tickets.title: Implement canonical serialisation and hashing of proposals
tickets.objective: A proposal has one canonical byte form and one SHA-256, stable across key order and Unicode forms.
tickets.scope: As stated in the objective and acceptance criteria; nothing beyond them.

FR-IMP-001.reason: Deferred by the specification itself (IR1.1 and the CN1.1 transition). A legacy vault import means real personal documents, which the current authorisation does not allow.
FR-IMP-001.revisit: After production readiness (SB-078) and a separate owner authorisation for real data

FR-IMP-002.reason: Deferred by the specification itself; depends on FR-IMP-001 and on real personal documents being authorised.

FR-IMP-003.reason: Deferred by the specification itself; a rollback of import batches has no meaning until imports exist.

FR-ING-010.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): there is no local inbox folder; sources arrive through the service and are stored as immutable objects.

FR-KNW-004.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): the Obsidian vault is an optional export, not an editing surface; changes enter as proposals and a re-import is validated, never synchronised.

FR-AGT-004.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): terminal approval tiers and channels are replaced by scoped connector tokens that cannot approve and an owner-authenticated approval surface.

FR-AGT-007.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): no local Claude Code operating workspace is installed; sessions reach the service through the remote connector.

FR-SEC-001.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): local path restrictions do not apply to a hosted service; every authorisation is enforced on the server.

FR-SEC-006.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): a hosted service is reached over the network by design; the controls are the single authenticated path, encryption and recorded regions.

FR-OPS-007.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): launchd is specific to the Mac, which the product no longer depends on; scheduled work runs in the service.

FR-OPS-009.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): there is no local operating home or vault skeleton to initialise; the environment is created by migrations (SB-023) and deployment (SB-071).

NFR-004.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): offline operation is replaced by a service that runs with no personal computer online, plus a complete export.

NFR-009.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): a zero-egress rule cannot hold for a hosted service; it is replaced by recorded and enforced regions and by the exfiltration limits.

NFR-020.reason: Superseded by the cloud-native architecture (CN1.1 transition assessment): macOS compatibility is no longer a requirement of the service; client compatibility is tested against the deployed connector (SB-073).
